punchline: Accountants whose parents sent them cash held about 57 percent of the net worth of accountants who got nothing.
thirty_sec: Stanley and Danko compared accountants. Those whose parents regularly gave them cash held about 57 percent of the net worth of those who got none. The authors say such gifts can create a false sense of security, and some recipients buy homes above their means. Critics note the study ignored people who lost money.
